title: A Terminal for the Horizon
premise: Sebastian Ishikawa investigates impossible accidents along the Relay, a chain of half-abandoned stations linking two human colonies that severed contact generations ago. When a name appears on the manifest of a ship that never launched, she traces it to a hidden cryo-ark holding the last frozen citizens of both worlds — and discovers the accident that 'killed' it was staged by factions on each side who want only their own people revived. As sabotage spreads and the ark's orbit decays, Sebastian, the resurrected stranger Mara Voss, and a ragtag crew of Relay outcasts must choose which half of humanity wakes. In the end Sebastian refuses the binary: she wakes them all in shifts, sacrificing her own berth, and the found family she built becomes the bridge the two worlds lost.
about_author: Paloma Thackeray is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade untangling disasters at sea before turning to fiction about disasters among the stars. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where she insists the fog improves her prose.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Investigating a cargo pod crash on station Meridian's End, Sebastian finds a shipping manifest listing a passenger — Mara Voss — aboard the Halcyon Reach, a vessel destroyed forty years ago and never flown since. The impossible paperwork unsettles her more than the wreck. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into dread as she realizes someone is forging history itself.

chapters.title: A Name Out of Cold Sleep
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, then Mara. Following the manifest to a decommissioned dry dock, Sebastian finds Mara Voss alive, freshly thawed, with no memory of how she boarded the Halcyon Reach. Mara remembers only a vote — everyone aboard choosing who would wake first. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two women who are each other's only evidence.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Fleeing Meridian's End ahead of whoever erased the ship, they book passage on Sebastian's regular hauler run down the Relay. Mara glimpses the liminal world of relay workers, smugglers, and station orphans who treat Sebastian as one of their own. Emotional beat: Mara's loneliness cracking open as she witnesses belonging she never had.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, No Words
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. At the mid-Relay hub, Sebastian pulls old records and learns the Halcyon Reach was the last joint project before the colonies cut contact — an ark meant to preserve both populations through a plague scare that never came. Someone on each side made sure it 'failed.' Emotional beat: grief for a cooperation that was murdered, not abandoned.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Confessed
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Diving the actual wreck site, Mara recovers a black box proving the destruction was ordered simultaneously by both governments — each believing the other side's sleepers were dead weight. The dive nearly kills her; Sebastian hauls her back. Emotional beat: trust sealed in vacuum, and the first admission that this is bigger than either of them.

chapters.title: The People Who Own the Silence
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The pair confronts Director Anselm Reyes, architect of the cover-up, now a beloved statesman. He offers Sebastian wealth and Mara a quiet life — if the ark stays lost. She refuses; hours later their safehouse burns. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of realizing justice has no institution left to appeal to.

chapters.title: Crew of the Unlisted
chapters.summary: POV Mara. With authorities hunting them, the Relay outcasts — a disgraced pilot, a station-born engineer, a medic who owes Sebastian her life — formally join them. They plan to reach the intact backup ark before Reyes's faction scuttles it. Emotional beat: the found family crystallizes, each member choosing the mission over safety.

chapters.title: Orbit Is a Countdown
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. They reach the backup ark to find its orbit already decaying and its systems rigged to fail — Reyes chose mutual erasure over shared truth. The crew races to stabilize the hull while Sebastian decrypts the wake-order protocols. Emotional beat: rising panic as every solution demands a sacrifice no one wants to name.

chapters.title: The Vote Again
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Cornered by Reyes's boarding party, the crew faces the original question: there is power to wake only half the sleepers before the ark breaks up. Mara proposes what the Halcyon's passengers never got — a real vote, alternating berths between both worlds, starting with the children. The crew holds the line while it runs. Emotional beat: defiant hope against arithmetic.

chapters.title: A Terminal for the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, closing with Mara. Sebastian gives up her own revival slot to power the final thaw cycle, waking the last shift as the ark is caught by a joint rescue flotilla — both worlds, shamed into cooperation by broadcast evidence. Reyes falls; the Relay reopens. Emotional beat: bittersweet homecoming — Sebastian sleeps, trusting the family she built to be there when she wakes.
